name: Better Planet Generation
summary: A huge planet generation overhaul that aims at making your hundreds of hours of exploration in the magnificent, infinite universe of No Man's Sky less repetitive and hopefully even more memorable.
author: WoodyMontana
description:
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][i][b]                                                     [size=6]Better Planet Generation[/size][/b][/i][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629738968-1312445652.jpeg[/img]

[size=4][b]More planets

[/b][size=3]Better Planet Generation is a total overhaul of the planetary generation in No Man's Sky.[/size] [size=3]It improves by a significant margin the procedural aspect of the universe while at the same time respecting the original work and vision from Hello Games.[/size]

[size=3]It adds thousands of new distinct environments to the universe[/size][/size]. All of them come in five different life levels and varying placement scales and layouts. These environments were made to seamlessly combine with each other in many different ways.

Better Planet Generation is designed to bring variety to the different biomes you will visit but most of all it brings a lot of variation to the universe. Outside of the countless combinations of assets and their resulting new environments, planets you visit will present themselves differently each time. Placement layouts, scale of the regions, density, variety of assets and their respective scale, ...

No planet will look exactly the same. Unless, of course, it is a very simple one. More on that below.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1631005159-472402214.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936034-1789086190.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1610300150-1298994048.jpeg[/img]


[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=4][b]Sub Biomes[/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Caves and underwater sub biomes have also been entirely overhauled.

Tons of new variants have been added underground and just like on the surface, additional objects can spawn to increase variety even more.

﻿[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410276-924973523.jpeg[/img]﻿

Underwater has been completely revamped and is now generated through a triple layered dynamic framework combining assets to generate highly varied and detailed environments.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629738939-165524032.jpeg[/img]
[b][size=4]
Unique planets

[/size][/b][size=4][size=3]On top of all the added variety, BPG also uses a flexible dynamic generation framework that can take many shapes[/size][/size] and create countless planetary variations, even when the same environments are being used multiple times.

Each planet generated has its own selection of parts based on its biome. Some liberties have been taken when designing and attributing those parts to the various biomes. Some objects have been injected to improve variety, but some restrictions have also been applied to preserve each biome's identity. Better Planet Generation also introduces countless restored, modified or repurposed assets to the game in order to increase the variety while preserving its visual style.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936068-132859967.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630936034-754906087.jpeg[/img]

[/size][/size][/size][/size]
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]Natural Generation[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Better Planet Generation is a vastly different experience compared to the unmodded game and even other biome mods.
Not even taking into account the small details, it is more than likely that you will never be able to encounter all the possible assets combinations this mod can generate. Let alone in the different regional layouts each dynamic template can result in.

Each biome has access to multiple procedural templates. Each producing different results in terms of layouts and objects combinations.
Their common goal is to show you a different kind of environment each time. Aesthetically and structurally.
No more "postcard" planets where most of what there is to see is right around the corner. The scale of the generation can get extremely vast compared to the vanilla game.

Planetary generation can now affect your visual enjoyment and the gameplay.
It is a video game, after all.

A world generated at its fullest possible level and highest complexity can take you some time to fully explore on foot. Meaning seeing the most notable regions (and not all of them) and scanning everything.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630052272-1155900954.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1610300150-2086924238.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630272224-118529207.jpeg[/img]
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]More Variation[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

On the other hand, Better Planet Generation also allows more simple, generic yet still visually interesting planets to see :

- Planets only covered in grass and some plants, rocks or both.
- More barren worlds dominated by giant stone or crystal spires.
- Radioactive wastelands.
- Planets dotted with trees or occasional small forests.
- Volcanic wastelands.
- Toxic fields.
- Rocky swamps.
- ...

And the list goes on and on.
[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3]The occurence of these "generic" planets only relies on probabilites. None of my templates is designed to specifically produce them.
I made sure they still looked good, though.[/size][/size][/size][/size]

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410296-1590906166.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1626079315-1486130072.jpeg[/img]

[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=4]Different Experience[/size][/b][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size][/size]

Better Planet Generation is not for everyone. Planets can be both very detailed in every aspect or very simple.
If you expect to always see trees and a full grass coverage on your Lush planet or anywhere else, there are other mods for that.
This is not what you should expect using BPG.

Now, whether you are a new player ready to explore an infinite universe or a more weathered one that wants to be surprised by the game again, I suggest you give Better Planet Generation a try. It won't harm your game in any way.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1629923717-282604290.jpeg[/img][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1634/images/797/797-1630410307-2137550589.jpeg[/img]

[size=5][size=3][size=4][size=3][b][size=5]WARNING BEFORE INSTALLING :[/size][/b]

Installing this mod will operate changes to the terrain in every biomes.
It is also recommended to install it while in a space station / anomaly / freighter and not on a planet's surface.
Some major updates to the mod can reset the terrain or biome lists.
I'll include a warning on the download page and the sticky when it's the case.[/size][/size][/size][/size]


Recommended :
[/size][/size]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/968]DUD's Sky - Colors[/url] : load planetary colour palettes before BPG to avoid procedural textures conflicts.
[/size][/size]

name: Balbrock's Mega Mods
summary: Mods compilation for improve gameplay and Fun
author: Balbrock
description:
===New version 05/2021===

Since many mods no longer work or cause bugs I thought I had to study it more closely.
I present you "Balbrock Mega Mods Pack" is a set of little things that aim to make the game less painful and a little more fun.
The mods include:
- An overall improvement in the speed of ships in [s]space and[/s] planets and a reduction in the cost to "take off" from it.
- [s]An increase in the amount of animals present on the planets as well as a small increase in their sizes.[/s]
- More fuel for the jet pack.
- Improvement of the blasting with the laser.
- Slight increase in weapon damage.
- [s]Increased running speed.[/s]
- [s]Random increase in the size of plants on planets from 1 to x3.[/s]
- Increase and improve the personal scan and the vessels.
- Improved plant growth rate in the base.
- Increased refinery speed.
- Increased storage stack of the character and ships.
- Increased range to com at your ship.
- Increased action button speed.
- Allows you to hover over planets.
- Torch improvement.

The goal is not to make a cheat mods but to improve the gameplay without destroying the player's feeling of progression.

The mod is in one file and works with the latest version of the game.
To install it, copy the file "Balbrock's Mega Mods.pak" in: C: / => Program Files => Steam => SteamApps => Common => No Man's Sky => GAMEDATA => PCBANKS => Mods.

> If the "Mods" folder does not exist, create one.
> !!!! Consider removing the text document "Disable Mods" in BCBANKS for it to work.

Sorry for my english and good game to all.

name: HD Space Planet Clouds 2.2
summary: High-Res planet clouds as seen from space
author: Lo2k
description:
This mod is an overhauled atmospheric cloud texture based on Scooterbaga 's [url=https://nomansskymods.com/mods/hd-clouds/][color=#f1c232]HD Clouds mod[/color][/url] 4K texture (8192x4096 pixels).

Scooterbaga's Nasa2 texture was very nice because it's a 4x version of the original game texture but looking at it more closely, I discovered it had a lot of issues here and there, so I did a big pass on it and tried to fix everything I noticed.

In details, this mod fixes the following issues from Scooterbaga's texture (see the last screenshot for a snapshot of my work) :
- removed a sometimes very visible seam appearing verticaly over all the planet at tiling position
- fixed tiling missmatch clouds
- filled holes, low transparency corrections and softened cloud cuts
- removed black dot lines, speckles and scratches
[color=#ffd966]
Note that it only improves long distance clouds as seen from space or from another planet, not the volumetric sky clouds.[/color]

Enjoy.

Optional :
- Add a slow pace rotation movement to your planet atmosphere with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1662][color=#f1c232]Rotating Atmosphere[/color][/url]

name: Exosolar's and Babs' Beyond Base Building
summary: ★ FULLY MP compatible, this mod adds an extreme degree of freedom to the vanilla base-building options
author: Exosolar Sparky NeptuneX3 Babscoole
description:
[b][color=#f1c232][size=4]What is this Mod?[/size][/color][/b]
[size=4]There are now almost 1,000 buildable base parts in vanilla No Man's Sky! It's a dream come true!
This mod adds an extreme degree of freedom to the vanilla base-building options.
This does NOT mean the mod gives you access to all buildable parts.  You still need to learn the blueprints for each.  :)
Beyond Base Building does NOT add any new build parts to the game.

Now includes all the functionality of gBase Items, [color=#ff0000]if chosen by running the Lua script[/color]:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Can multiply power, extraction, and storage rates by 2, 5, or 10. WARNING: Bases built with this mod cannot be uploaded for multiplayer when using 2x, 5x, or 10x multiplied rates.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[list]
[*][size=4]EM Generators do not need a hotspot and produce 250 power.  Not enabled by default.  Must run Lua through ANUMSS and answer question "Choose a multiplier for Storage and Rates and EMAnywhere status" to generate custom mod file to enable.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]

It is [b]fully compatible[/b] with multiplayer, co-op building, uploading, etc, because it [i]does not add[/i] any parts, which would cause issues in multiplayer.[/size]

[size=4][color=#f1c232][b]★ Beyond Basebuilding[/b] is fully Lua scripted, with script provided for easy updating and merging [b]★[/b][/color] and carries over all of the official updates and improvements offered by Hello Games [b]plus[/b]:[/size]

[list]
[*][size=4]Most parts can be Scaled [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] prefab building parts, [color=#fff2cc]Exocraft Geobays, Mineral/Gas Extractors and Base Computer[/color] (Door attachment points bug out when scaled, and issues persist with scaled base computers and geobays).  There may be others not listed.  Be aware, scaling breaks snapping.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Many parts can be built in a Freighter.  [color=#fff2cc][i]Exceptions[/i][/color]  include the Base Computer, Industrial Mining parts, Vehicle Summoners and planet-based teleporter.[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Many parts can be built at a Planetary Base [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] the freighter teleporter and the Orbital Exocraft Materialiser[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts can be built above and below water[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts can change color and material[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]All parts, which can be deleted, can be deleted without also deleting attached objects [color=#fff2cc][i]except[/i][/color] Decals and Posters[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]No build-count limits [i][color=#fff2cc]except[/color][/i] for parts related to resources harvesting, certain terminals, beacons and message capsules (and others with limits that are hard coded into the game, as they are added or changed by Hello Games).[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Unlimited Storage Containers[color=#cccccc][size=3][i]—*This does not increase actual storage amounts: Each numbered container acts as an index to the store rather than a physical box[/i][/size][/color][/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Foundation, Pavings and Communications Station can be placed anywhere (not only on bare terrain)[/size][/*]
[*][size=4]Non corvette parts buildable with corvettes[/size][/*]
[/list][size=4]
Some customization of the mod is available just by running it through AMUMSS, where you'll be prompted about enabling several feature.  Even more customization can be had by editing the top portion of the Lua before processing.  See Lua usage below for link to AMUMSS install and basic usage How to.[/size]

[color=#f1c232][b][u][size=5]Disclaimer:[/size][/u][/b][/color]
[size=3]This MOD makes changes to the placement and usage setting of vanilla parts.  If the MOD is removed, the vanilla settings will be restored and parts that "violate" a vanilla setting as well as those connected may go "poof".  Best practice is to regularly backup your saves for semi-painless recovery from the unexpected.[/size]

[size=5][u][b][color=#f1c232]Is this Mod up-to-date?[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[size=4][i][b]Any mod files which are not hidden or demoted to the "Old Files" area can be expected to work.[/b][/i]
All uploaded files (on the Files page) are maintained with their packing date and version of the MBINCompiler used to pack it. Older mod versions, no longer compatible with the current version of No Man's Sky will be demoted to the "Old Files" subsection, but will remain available for download. There are no side-effects to using this mod.[/size]

[size=4][u][b][color=#f1c232]How to update, tweak, combine, or patch the mod with AMUMSS?[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[size=4]As this mod is now Lua scripted, you can [color=#fff2cc]easily [b]update[/b], [b]tweak[/b] or [b]merge[/b] the mod yourself[/color] (if a game update breaks this PAK of the mod, or you have other PAK or Lua mods that could conflict with this one). [color=#cccccc][size=3][i]—*Click on the spoiler below for more[/i][/size][/color][/size]
[spoiler]
[size=3][u]Notes on AMUMSS:[/u]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url] tries to update [url=https://github.com/monkeyman192/MBINCompiler/releases]MBINcompiler[/url] automatically. If it fails to convert EXML/MBIN files, its likely due to a very recent NMS version update and MBINcompiler is awaiting an update too.
If so, I highly recommend you to disable your mods and wait for MBINCompiler to be updated (it's pretty quick in general).[/size]


[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Updating the mod after a game update:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][list]
[*] [size=3]Download [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957]AMUMSS[/url], and extract it locally,  avoid placing the AMUMSS folder in a path with special characters or in a system folder like [color=#fff2cc][i]"C:\Program Files (x86)\(...)"[/i][/color].[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Place the mod Lua script (only the .LUA file, not the .PAK file) in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]AMUMSS will normally auto-detect the NMS installation folder, but you can also manually edit the path in the [color=#fff2cc][i]NMS_FOLDER.txt[/i][/color] file.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root of the AMUMSS folder and follow the steps, selecting the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]A new modded PAK file will be created, using the last update of the MBIN game files duly amended by the script.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=3]Most of the time simply recompiling the mod using the Lua script will make it compatible again. Use the latest script to ensure you adopt any mod adjustments to accommodate the latest NMS build.[/size][size=3] There are two main causes of mods not correctly updating with this method:
1) MBINCompiler needs an update to be able to decompile the latest version of the game MBIN files.
2) Structural changes have been made to the MBIN files called by this Lua script. Whilst unlikely, this will require some script rewrite and other mods are likely affected.[/size][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Tweaking the mod:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]Use the same process as described in [color=#fff2cc][i]Updating the mod[/i][/color].
Just modify the script as you want before recompiling it. Look at the top of my scripts, you can generally edit modifiers there, or even disable/enable some features very easily.[/size]

[size=3][color=#cccccc][i]*[url=https://notepad-plus-plus.org/]Notepad++[/url] or [url=https://code.visualstudio.com/download/]VSCode[/url] are generally recommended to read EXML and Lua files, due to large file support and automatic highlighting. The [url=https://sourceforge.net/projects/npp-compare/]Compare plugin[/url] for Notepad++, and Lua is also a must-have to highlight file differences.[/i][/color][/size][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Combining mods that provide Lua scripts:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]You'll want to do this if multiple mods affect the same MBIN file.[/size]

[list]
[*] [size=3]Place all the scripts in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Follow the step, selecting that you want to combine all the scripts into one PAK file, and the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[/list]
[size=3]AMUMSS will output a PAK file that will contain the modifications of all the scripts.[/size]
[color=#cccccc][size=3][i]*If the scripts modify the exact same values in the MBIN file, the last loaded script will overwrite the preceding script values.[/i][/size][/color][/spoiler]

[size=3][u][b][color=#f1c232]Patch in the mod to make it compatible with other PAK files:[/color][/b][/u][/size]
[spoiler][size=3]You will want to do this if another mods isn't Lua scripted, and affects the same MBIN file as the Lua scripted mod.

It will work when :
Case 1) you patch a Lua scripted mod for only one other PAK.
Case 2) you patch a Lua scripted mod for several other PAKs, but only if the other PAKs don't modify the same MBIN files between them.[/size]

[size=3][b]How to create a patched PAK:[/b][/size]

[list]
[*] [size=3]Copy the script and the other mod(s) PAK(s) in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder of AMUMSS.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Launch [color=#fff2cc][i]BUILDMOD.bat[/i][/color] in the root folder of AMUMSS, and follow the steps, selecting the option to automatically install it in the NMS [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder.[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]The new PAK file will contain all the Lua script modifications, and a compatibility patch for the other mod(s) PAK(s).[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Rename it something like [color=#fff2cc][i]"__zzz Scripted Mod Name -Patched For- The Other Mod Name.pak"[/i][/color].[/size]
[size=3][color=#fff2cc][i]"__zzz"[/i][/color] prefix is to ensure that it'll be loaded after the mod(s) it was patched for (for NMS loading order, underscore [i]"_"[/i] came after every other characters).[/size][/*]
[*][size=3]Remove the original scripted mod PAK from the [color=#fff2cc][i]MODS[/i][/color] folder, and copy both the new patched one, and the other mod(s) PAK(s), into it.[/size][/*]
[/list][size=3][u]Notes:[/u]
[b]Be sure the mod PAK you want to create a compatibility patch for, is updated for the latest NMS version.[/b]
-> When AMUSS find an MBIN file affected by a script and by a PAK in the [color=#fff2cc][i]ModScript[/i][/color] folder, it will take the MBIN file from the mod PAK over the original one of the game, and will apply to it the modifications listed in the script.
So, if the MBIN file of the mod PAK is not updated, the one in the resulting patched PAK won't be either.[/size][/spoiler]
[/spoiler]

[center][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/images/1634/95741288-1598421367.png[/img][/center]

[size=4]All the erroneous limitations in building are pretty silly, aren't they? In making this mod, I paid specific attention to making sure I did not make changes that will invalidate the bases built with it from online play. Any base made with Beyond BaseBuilding will be fully viable and visible in online play, even when other players don't have this mod! name: Better Rewards
summary: Increase the amount of currency you get with faster word learning and increased resource gathering options. Frigate (Freighter) Expeditions are also included!
author: MrTrack
description:
Better Rewards increases the amount of units, nanite clusters and quicksilver you get from completing missions or interacting with objects in the world. Non npc word learning (such as knowledge stones and dictionaries) is also faster.

[color=#bf9000][size=3]IMPORTANT NOTE: Don't use this mod when I haven't updated it to the new game version (especially when it is a new or returning expedition)
[/size][/color][color=#bf9000]if you really want to use it when I haven't updated it yet, make sure you [/color][color=#bf9000]back up your save[/color][color=#bf9000] or build the mod using the lua scripts yourself.[/color]

[b]Currency[/b]

Currency gain is roughly increased by 5 times, so as to make it a viable option besides crafting and selling valuable trading goods. Some unit values were tremendously increased (eg.: from minimum amount of 1000-2000 to 20000-50000) like the terminals in abandoned settlements to make the early game less grindy.

Includes:
[list]
[*]Space station missions and Nexus missions
[*]Interactable objects/devices (abandoned buildings, damaged machinery, waypoints, etc.)
[*]Sentinels
[*]Alien interactions
[/list]
[b]Words[/b]

Learning words from non npc interactions (knowledge stones and dictionaries) is also 3 times faster (3 words learned form a single knowledge stone). You now also learn 5 Atlas words, instead of 1 and also have a chance (15%) to learn them when interacting with non npc learning sources.

[b]Resources

[/b]When gathering with the mining beam you generally get 2 times more resources (but only when the things explode as you mine them). Also includes containers, depots, guild rewards, asteroids and ships that drop resources.

[b]Frigate (Freighter) Expedition Rewards

[/b]After a successful expedition, when collecting your rewards you get 5x more units and nanites, 2x more products like Storage Augmentation and NipNip Buds and 3x more resources like Copper, Emeril and Cadmium.
[b]
Installation

[/b]Make sure you delete or edit DISABLEMODS.TXT in your game library (...\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS) before trying to use mods. Extract the zip file to ...\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS folder and you are good to go (Create MODS folder if you don't have one). Alternatively you can just use Vortex to download and install.

This mod modifies the [color=#ff0000][size=3]REWARDTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color] and [color=#ff0000][size=3]EXPEDITIONREWARDTABLE.MBIN[/size][/color] file and will not work with other mods that use those tables.

[b]Updated to NMS version 6.21 (Build ID: 21918502) on 2026.02.13.[/b]

name: Black Space 4.3
summary: Makes space much darker
author: Lo2k
description:
This mod replaces fully colored space by a more common black space.

You can choose between 2 versions :
  - Black Space : Pure black space, white suns, no nebulae
  - Black Space + Nebulae : Black space but colored suns and colored nebulae

Since 2.2B, you can now also remove the too numerous stars from the sky with the No Stars optional mod (there's sadly no available slider yet in the game to just reduce the amount of stars visible in the sky).


Enjoy.

Optional : 
- Enjoy black space even more with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1084][color=#ffd966]No Space Dust and No Space Plasma[/color][/url]
- Enjoy black space without bloom everywhere with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2315][color=#ffd966]No Bloom Effect[/color]
[/url]- Enjoy Station and other indoor place independent of (black) space color with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/2440][color=#ffd966]Indoors Lighting Fix[/color][/url]

[color=#ffd966]
News in v4.3 : No Star was updated for 6.45 game version. Both Black Space mods are still fine as 3.0.[/color]

[size=2]Compatibility : [/size]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/880][color=#ffd966]- [u]CHECK IF THIS MOD IS COMPATIBLE WITH LATEST GAME VERSION[/u][/color][/url]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/articles/85][color=#f6b26b]- [u]CHECK IF THIS MOD NEEDS TO BE MERGED WITH ANOTHER OF MY MODS[/u][/color][/url]
These mods edit the following files :
    - METADATA\SIMULATION\SOLARSYSTEM\WEATHER\SKYSETTINGS\SPACESKYCOLOURS.MBIN
    - METADATA\SIMULATION\SOLARSYSTEM\WEATHER\SKYSETTINGS\SPACERARESKYCOLOURS.MBIN


Credits : Thanks to Rayrod who pointed me toward the right files now that shaders can't be edited anymore.

name: Chromatic Expansion
summary: Reintroduction of the Chromatic Expansion bug.
author: Slaymeister
description:
There was a bug that allowed you to create unlimited amounts of four elements - Copper, Indium, Emeril, and Cadmium.  You could use 1 unit of the element and 1 Chromatic Metal to create 4 of the source element.  You could then turn right around and create more Chromatic Metal using 2 or less of the created elements at a net gain.  Some of the elements created more Chromatic Metal than the others depending on their rarity, with Indium being the most efficient.

The interwebs got all excited about this bug and the associated exploit, even christening it the "Chromatic Expansion". You can Google it.  It was a thing. Actually, people crying like whiny little babies about missing this exploit would probably be one of the top hits, based on what I found, because it got patched somewhere along the line. Point at the small minded people crying and whining like little babies. Laugh mockingly at their ridiculous hysteria. Your mockery is the only way they'll learn.

So anyway, I completely missed this exploit, and I was crying hysterically like a whiny little baby about it. Okay, maybe I'm being hyperbolic about the sentiment around this, but I definitely did grunt disapprovingly, and I'm standing by that one. That's when I threw together this mod to reintroduce the Chromatic Expansion exploit.

Modifies NMS_REALITY_GCRECIPETABLE and will conflict with any other mod that also targets this file.

This mod is perfect for using that mod scripting engine thingy so it doesn't get out of date.  Someone should totally steal this idea and make a version that plugs into that.

name: NomNom
summary: NomNom is the most complete savegame editor for NMS but also shows you additional information around the data you're about to change. author: zencq
description:
[color=#e69138][size=3][b]NomNom is now in beta state.[/b] This means for you that some things may still not be 100% finished but the general state of the tool is a lot better than before.[/size] If you encounter bugs or when you think something doesn't work as expected or could be improved, [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1566?tab=bugs]let me know[/url]![/color]

[color=#ff0000]All available features are tested while implemented but mistakes can happen, so be aware of that and backup your saves![/color]

The features can be divided into the different main parts:
[list]
[*][b]Manager[/b] Manage your saves!
[list]
[*]Automatic backup.[/*]
[*]Save your save as human-readable JSON.[/*]
[*]Copy, move, and swap slots to another.[/*]
[*]Delete your save.[/*]
[/list][/*]
[*][b]Editor[/b] Edit your save for your needs!
[list]
[*]Ability to manage fleets, change data values like currencies and stats, and organize inventories.[/*]
[*]Ability to fast travel to any system you like, trigger space battles, and clear portal interference.[/*]
[*]Ability to edit your knowledge and recorded experiences.[/*]
[/list][/*]
[/list]
Have a look at the screenshots as well, to see what NomNom is capable of.

Each version of NomNom is built with the latest game version (at that time) in mind and the version number is reflecting that. Each one is also backwards
compatible down to [b]Beyond 2.11[/b] and even saves before that can still be edited via the build-in JSON editor. If you use it with a newer game version branch than
the one it was built for (e.g. [b]7.00[/b]), things should work as usual in most cases but there can always be a breaking change.

NomNom is compatible with every platform No Man's Sky is available on (some work better than others though). You can select a specific account/folder with you saves or, for platforms on PC, one level above if you have multiple accounts. A complete and always up-to-date overview with additional notes can be found [url=https://github.com/zencq/libNOM.io?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-started]on GitHub[/url].


[b]Instructions[/b]
[list=1]
[*]After downloading and extracting the zip file you'll find a few files. All you need to care about is the executable ([b]NomNom.exe[/b]) but new folders may    be created at runtime (e.g. for backups) that will become relevant to you.[/*]
[*]You may want to create a shortcut to the executable for easier access.[/*]
[*]As the tool includes an automatic backup functionality you don't need to do it manually but if you want to be absolutely safe, do it.[/*]
[*]At first start the tool locates your saves at the default location of each platform but if that fails, you must select it manually.[/*]
[*]Select a slot.[/*]
[*]Start tinkering![/*]
[/list]

If you like NomNom and want to support me in its further development, you can do so via the donation options above or on [url=https://www.buymeacoffee.com/cengelha]Buy Me a Coffee[/url], [url=https://github.com/sponsors/cengelha]GitHub[/url], [url=https://ko-fi.com/cengelha]Ko-fi[/url], and [url=https://www.patreon.com/cengelha]Patreon[/url]. I will appreciate it!
There won't be a paywall though.

The is also a dedicated [url=https://discord.gg/nomnom-762409407488720918]Discord[/url] server where you'll find all information in one place, firsthand. Please read the rules first, to gain full access. If you need (or want to offer) help, found a bug, have a suggestion, or something else regarding NomNom, you will find, or can post it there.

Issues created here on Nexus Mods or via another channel will of course also be addressed.

name: Gnome Ann's Dusks - 1000 New Sunsets
summary: Adds 1,000 thoughtfully generated sunsets to the game (vanilla only has 1)! Part of the Gnome Ann's Sky mod family. Works with Expeditions
author: Dr Kaii
description:
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1428][img]data:image/png;base64,[/img][/url]   [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1848/][img]data:image/png;base64,[/img][/url]
<br />
<br />[color=#ff0000][size=4][b]First update in 1k downloads! Now working with Aquarius[/b][/size][/color]
<br />
<br />This mod, while works on its own, is best combined with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1428]Gnome Ann's Sky[/url]﻿, a mod that adds 100,000 new skies to the game (base game currently only uses 6 skies for all original planets, and a handful more for Lava and Swamp biomes). You can also bolt on [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1848/]1,000 Gnome Ann's Nights[/url], which adds 1,000 nights to the game!
<br />
<br />Like [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1428]Gnome Ann's Sky[/url], Gnome Ann's Dusks adds 1,000 custom skies to the game, generated from a hand-tuned algorithm, using custom software I wrote to produce the colours and visualise and tweak the results. The key theme is "variation". While most of the skies are geared to be stunningly beautiful, and would fit well alongside vanilla palettes, being very tame, no colours are truly ruled out and you can, in keeping with the feel of the game, never truly know what to expect next!
<br />
<br />The algorithm produces colours in various levels of "rarity", so keep hunting for that incredible sunset that [url=https://xkcd.com/1704/]Gnome Ann[/url]﻿ has imagined before!
<br />
<br />[u]Philosophy[/u]
<br />[list]
<br />[*]After seeing that the sunset on Mars is blue, and noticing that EVERY planet in No Man's Sky, regardless of its sky colour, has the exact same, earthy red/orange sunset, I set out to make my own. 
<br />[*]It's created under the assumption that almost any colour combinations are possible for sunsets, which is scientifically plausible. Expect not just the beautiful, but the very alien too. 
<br />[*]I will strive to keep the sunsets exactly the same, i.e. the sunsets on your favourite planets will always remain the same! (unless HG bork things)
<br />[/list]
<br />[u]Instructions[/u]
<br />[list]
<br />[*]This mod can be installed on its own, it [u]does not[/u] require any other mods, (not even [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/1428]Gnome Ann's Sky[/url]). 
<br />[*]Simply extract the DRKAII_GnomeAnnsDusks1K[Next Gen].pak into your MODS folder. 
<br />[*]If you haven't got this, go to C:\...\Steam Library\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS and make a MODS folder and stick the mod in there. Then go back up a level to the PCBANKS folder and rename the DISABLEMODS.TXT to something else
<br />[/list][u][size=2]Files Used By This Mod[/size][/u]
<br />METADATA\SIMULATION\SOLARSYSTEM\WEATHER\SKYSETTINGS\DUSKSKYCOLOURS.MBIN
<br />
<br />[size=4][color=#cc0000][b]Looking for fellow Gnome Ann's Sky explorers? Join the discord[/b][/color]: [url=https://discord.gg/eefk3eJ]https://discord.gg/eefk3eJ
<br />
<br />
<br />[/url][/size]NOTE! I am also working on a mod to add 1,000 [i]night [/i]skies to the game, in the same theme. They have been generated in the same way. Check the miscellaneous files and please offer feedback.

name: Almost Perfect Flight
summary: Changes Ship Flight and Landing Characteristics within Planet Atmospheres and Space.
author: Silent369
description:
[center][size=6][b]Almost Perfect
Flight v5.8[/b][/size][/center]
[quote][b]Ship flight and landings in NMS have always troubled me. So, after much experimenting I offer this humble mod for your enjoyment[/b][/quote]

[b]Notes[/b]:
There are now also two versions of [b]Almost Perfect Flight[/b]. A [u][b]Lite[/b][/u] version with less aggressive multipliers for those who prefer a closer to vanilla experience and is the recommended version to use. [b]Mini-warping will now disengage when entering a planet atmosphere so you should no longer impact the terrain :) [/b]

[b]Lite Boosts[/b]
[quote][code]boostMult = 1.25
boostMxSp = 2.5
speedMult = 1.5
thrstMult = 1.5
warpSMult = 2.2[/code][/quote]
And the Full version retaining all the previous settings with the following multipliers applied. This can be a little twitchy depending on your ships manoeuvrability bonus.

[b]Full Boosts[/b]
[quote][code]_boostMult = 1.5
_boostMxSp = 2.0
_speedMult = 2.5
_thrstMult = 1.5
_warpSMult = 2.5[/code][/quote]
[b]Hopefully these changes will cater to both those whom enjoy a 'closer to vanilla' experience with the benefit of 'hover-in-place' and much smoother landings. And those who just want fast ships, hover-in-place, softer landings with 'slightly' overclocked multipliers to get around just that bit quicker)[/b]

Optional No Reverse versions are now available for both Almost Perfect Flight Lite / Full.

Provides the following changes:
[quote][list]
[*]Boost Multipliers (Optional)[/*]
[*]Min Speed (0.01) (Optional)[/*]
[*]Launch Cost (30%) (Optional)[/*]
[*]Allows Hovering in Atmosphere[/*]
[*]Allows Reverse in Atmosphere[/*]
[*]Landing Curves Modified[/*]
[*]Remove Mini Warp Metric Lines[/*]
[*]Altitude that triggers Solar Sails Anim[/*]
[*]Speed at which Solar Sails Open / Close[/*]
[*]Aligns Anomaly to your ship when called[/*]
[/list][/quote]
Modifies: [u][b]GCSPACESHIPGLOBALS.GLOBAL.MBIN[/b][/u]

[quote][b][size=3]Installing No Man's Sky Mods[/size][/b] (Steam).

[b][u]Default Steam installation location:[/u][/b]
C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS

[b][u]Custom Steam installation location:[/u][/b]
E:\Steam\steamapps\common\No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS

1. Browse to the "No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA" folder.
2. Ensure there is a folder named MODS (Uppercase!) within, if not create it!
3. Place the <modname> folder into the GAMEDATA\MODS folder.
4. (Not necessary but can help when installing new mods).
    Optionally delete the file: GCMODSETTINGS.MXML from No Man's Sky\Binaries\SETTINGS
    It will be auto-regenerated with a new load order based on the mods you have)

If done correctly the game will display a MOD Warning Page: [u]Click to continue[/u].
You should now be presented with your save games list to choose from to start playing.[/quote]
Made with [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/957][i]AMUMSS[/i][/url]. Check my other [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/users/122177308?tab=user+files]MODS[/url].
Lua's included in the main download. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

The Waypoint update brought a new feature called auto-saving.
It is fine for players as it saves anywhere at anytime, even in your ship.

summary: Increases the material cost required to craft all products in No Man's Sky. Choose from x2 up to x100 crafting difficulty
author: azunain
description:
[center][size=6][b]HardcoreSky - Increased Crafting Costs[/b][/size]
[i]Tested for: No Man’s Sky 6.0.1 (Public)[/i][/center]

This mod increases the [b]material costs[/b] for crafting products, making crafting more deliberate and resource-driven. It scales the [b]Requirements → Amount[/b] of each product recipe in the crafting grid. Release is [b]EXML-based[/b] and includes the original [b].lua[/b] for AMUMSS users.

[line]
[size=4]🛠️ What’s new[/size]
[list]
[*]Updated for game version [b]6.0.1[/b].
[*][b]EXML override[/b] distribution (no .pak); [b].lua[/b] included for reproducibility.
[*]Global multiplier to crafting inputs with a curated exclusion pass to avoid soft-locks.
[/list]

[line]
[size=4]🔥 Choose Your Challenge Level[/size]
Each download applies a global multiplier to crafting requirements:
[list]
[*]🟢 [b]x2[/b] – Slight bump in effort
[*]🟡 [b]x5[/b] – Think before you craft
[*]🟠 [b]x10[/b] – Crafting takes real prep
[*]🔴 [b]x20[/b] – Every item has a weight
[*]🔴 [b]x50[/b] – High-stakes crafting
[*]🟥 [b]x100[/b] – The HardcoreSky way
[/list]

[line]
[size=4]🌍 What’s affected[/size]
[list]
[*]All craftable products defined in:
[code]METADATA/REALITY/TABLES/NMS_REALITY_GCPRODUCTTABLE.MBIN[/code]via their [b]Requirements → Amount[/b].[*]Typical items like Metal Plating, Launch Fuel, Life Support Gel, Microprocessors, Antimatter Housing, Wiring Loom alternatives, etc.
[*]Overall resource planning and supply-chain pacing.
[/list]

❌ [b]Explicitly not changed / Excluded on purpose[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Atlas Seeds[/b] ([i]ATLAS_SEED_1 … ATLAS_SEED_10[/i]) — left at vanilla cost
[*][b]Technology installation costs[/b] (separate mod)
[*][b]Base building part costs[/b] and Salvaged Data unlocks (separate mods)
[*][b]Environmental/hazard settings[/b], trade prices, or economy values
[*][b]Non-craftable / special-case products[/b], such as:
[list]
[*]Mission or story-only items and unique keys (e.g. ruins/derelict/security keys, quest-gated items)
[*]Seasonal/Expedition, Twitch/Promotional reward items
[*]Placeholders or unreleased/test entries present in the table but not normally crafted by players
[/list][/list]
[i]The exclusion pass avoids soft-locking quests and keeps limited-time or reward-only items intact.[/i]

[line]
[size=4]🧩 Technical[/size]
Edits:
[code]METADATA/REALITY/TABLES/NMS_REALITY_GCPRODUCTTABLE.MBIN[/code]
Method: multiply each product’s
[code]Requirements/Amount[/code]
by the selected factor. Exclusions are filtered out before applying changes. Distributed as [b]EXML[/b] (the included [b].lua[/b] mirrors these edits for AMUMSS).

[line]
[size=4]🗂️ Files edited (via EXML override)[/size]
[code]
METADATA/REALITY/TABLES/NMS_REALITY_GCPRODUCTTABLE.MBIN
[/code]

[line]
[size=4]⚠️ Compatibility[/size]
Incompatible with other mods that also modify:
[code]METADATA/REALITY/TABLES/NMS_REALITY_GCPRODUCTTABLE.MBIN[/code]

[line]
[size=4]🛠️ Installation (EXML)[/size]
1) Create (if missing):
[code]No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS[/code]
2) Remove/rename (if present):
[code]No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\PCBANKS\DISABLEMODS.TXT[/code]
3) Extract the chosen archive. Inside you’ll find a folder like:
[code]HardcoreSky_ProductCost_x10[/code]
4) Drop that folder into:
[code]No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS[/code]
[i]Example of final path (EXML override):[/i]
[code]No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS\HardcoreSky_ProductCost_x10\METADATA\REALITY\TABLES\NMS_REALITY_GCPRODUCTTABLE.EXML[/code]
[i]The included [b].lua[/b] is optional and provided for AMUMSS users.[/i]

[size=3][color=#ffff00]My Thanks to those of you who voted this Mod of the Month for July 2025.[/color]

[color=#ff0000][b]This is a quick fix for NMS 6.2 compatibility. A few custom parts are missing, but this mod is fully functional. I need to recreate the custom parts once the tools I use have been updated. [/b][/color][/size]

[size=3][u]zBest Freighter[/u] replaces the freighter bridge with an open-plan design and improved ergonomics. It expands the freighter hangar from 9 to 12 fully functional landing pads. The number of your starships that can be in the hangar is increased from 6 to 9. NPC ships and your friends (also using this mod) can use any/all of the unoccupied landing pads. The Corvette teleporters have been moved to a much more convenient location. There is also a Starship Outfitting terminal in the hanger.

A key aspect of this mod is the ability for you to build any object that can be built in your freighter base on your new bridge! You can now take full control of what YOUR fighter bridge looks like. Need more light? Add one. Want a conference table with chairs? Add them. You are limited only by your available blueprints and imagination. Since you can't remove things added by this mod, only a minimal set of items come pre-installed and they retain the flavor of the original bridge design elements.[/size]

[size=3][u][b][color=#00ff00]Details:[/color][/b][/u]
zBest Freighter combines and extends my 3 Freighter mods (zBridge, zBridge Terminal, and zHangar) This combination was required to enable increasing the landing pads in the hangar from 9 to 12. If you want to efficiently add lights to your new bridge add my zLights mod and use the completely new Lab Light. All of my mods now work on all freighters: capital, system, and pirate! You may wish to read the documentation for these individual mods as each goes into more detail.

[u][color=#ff7700][b]Special Note to Pirate Dreadnought Captains:[/b][/color][/u]
There are a few cosmetic issues with the Hangar interior on dreadnoughts. To save 50-100 hours of additional work, I decided to reuse the regular hanger interior on dreadnoughts.  And while it is fully functional, there are some issues in 3 of the 4 corners (fit and intrusions) that do not meet my standards. If there is enough interest in this mod, I do intend to completely redo the pirate hangar interior using the original pirate hangar 3D model parts. Frankly I'm a bit burned out with working on this right now and it may very well be August before I release a new version with that fix. Between now and then, I am open to suggestions on what items to add or remove on Dreadnoughts. Just leave a post.

This mod also patches 2 globals files. GcFleetGlobals is changed to increase the number of your starships that can be in the hangar from 6 to 9, increasing it to 10 may cause a crash on reload, increasing to to 11 or 12 will cause the game to fail to load. Changes to GcAiSpaceshipGlobals allows NPC ships to use ALL landing pads. When you visit the space station or a trading post, you will see more NPC ships landing than the usual 4 or 5. Both of these simple text files are in the mod's Globals folder and can be edited.

Anything you build and place on your bridge is part of your freighter base and counts against its 3000 part limit. These additions will remain if you should uninstall this mod. So you may need to manage those additions carefully. As with any of the bridge mods out there, you probably don't want to be standing on your bridge when you exit the game and uninstall any bridge replacement mod. You can end up trapped inside the old bridge structure. The game provides an emergency relocation option if you find yourself caught on your freighter.

Unlike almost all mods, the items zBest Freighter allows you place on your bridge can be seen by any other players who visit your bridge. The base parts you added will be seen by visitors just like any other part of your base. The placement may not make sense to the visitor unless they are also using zBest Freighter (as that piece is strictly local to the individual player). Said differently, if you and your friends all use zBest Freighter, each can customize their bridge and that custom bridge will be seen when you/they visit. With other bridge mods, every bridge you visit looks exactly like your own - because the effects of the mod are completely local to your computer.[/size]

[size=3][u]Before you report a bug:
[/u]NMS v6 is still very buggy. Freighter doors don't always open and One NPC ship may "land" above the hangar landing pad 2A. I have run into both of these "features" without the mod. NMS also has a VRAM memory leak that may cause low frame rates and or game crashes. All of this will likely be fixed in future NMS updates.[/size]

[size=3][u][color=#ff0000][b]Known Issues:[/b][/color][/u]
The original 3D model parts that the bridge and hangar are constructed from have numerous errors. I have fixed some of them, but many remain. You may never notice them all, but there are a couple that are more obvious. The elbows in each corridor from the hangar to the bridge have light leaks. You may also encounter a brief hang when entering those corners. I have not been able to track down the cause - yet. If you find your self walking around on the outside of your freighter, there are a couple of places where you may find yourself falling through the structure. Again, I have not fully tracked down the cause. This is not the mod's fault, it is a model deficiency. There are some limitations to modifying the 3D models and you may bump into some things that are not visible (all in places you are unlikely to frequent). I take full responsibility for degrading the fit and finish of the exterior of the bridge. I had to refit the pieces HG provided to improve the interior appearance at the expense of exterior.

This mod is of limited scope, replacing/enhancing the freighter Bridge and Hangar, including the Bridge Terminal. This mod is not compatible with any other mods that replace or edit these files. The mod that loads last is the one you will see in effect. The [color=#00ffff]!zBest Freighter[/color] folder should be placed in your No Man’s Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS folder along with all of your other mods.

[u][b][color=#00ff00]Important Note:[/color][/b][/u]
If you are currently using zBridge, zBridge Terminal, and/or zHangar, (Thank you! and) you will need to uninstall these mods since zBest Freighter replaces all three.

[u][b][color=#00ff00]Highly recommended mods for use with zBest Freighter (You really want to add these to your mods):[/color][/b][/u]
zLights: Superior lights for use in your base - one light may be all you need.
Exosolar's Beyond Base Building: Allows you to build almost anything anywhere.

[color=#ffff00]This mod would not be possible without the use of the fabulous MBINcompiler and NMSDK plug-in for Blender.
A special thank you to the senior modders on the No Man's Sky Modding Discord for their patience and guidance.[/color]

[color=#00ff00]I hope you find this mod useful and enjoy it.  If you do like this mod and were waiting for this update, I ask that you consider taking a moment to endorse it. Endorsements are the only real feedback that is reliable.

Cheers, JMZ[/color][/size]

name: Subnautica PDA Exosuit Voice
summary: This mod replaces the default exosuit voice with the voice of the Subnautica PDA. Of course, of the first Subnautica.
author: Legandy
description:
I love Subnautica and No Man's Sky feels like space Subnautica.
One of Subnautica's charm was the PDA and the sometimes funny and iconic lines.
This charm of an AI assistant is not present in NMS.
I felt nostalgic so I made that exosuit replacement.


[b][u][size=3]How I created it:[/size][/u][/b]
I got most of the voice lines from [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/168?tab=description]Custom voices guide[/url], the rest I transcribed myself [url=https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1iJITjDQPowqthtOQ1yQ2GJlxNoG69EX-0iK6lBr8Wzk/edit?usp=sharing]NMS Voice Lines[/url].
You can find the Original and the Subnautica themed lines in the sheet.
I'm open for better changes to the lines, just add a comment to the corresponding voice line and leave a comment here.
First I tried to use the Original TTS Amy Voice and Audacity but wasn't satisfied with the result and the scaleability would have consumed more time than I wanted.
Then I remembered [url=https://github.com/OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl]Piper TTS[/url].
I searched for a voice model on [url=https://huggingface.co/]Hugging Face[/url] and I gladly found a voice model for [url=https://huggingface.co/Aquaaa123/piper-tts-pda-subnautica]Subnautica PDA[/url].
I wrote a [url=https://github.com/Legandy/csv2PiperTTS]csv2PiperTTS script[/url] that uses a user created voice_lines.csv (exported from a two column spreadsheet, example in the [url=https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1iJITjDQPowqthtOQ1yQ2GJlxNoG69EX-0iK6lBr8Wzk/edit?usp=sharing]sheet[/url]) that does all the job from TTS, speed control and loudness correction.
After that, I converted the .wav files to .wem files with the [url=https://github.com/khossyy/wem2ogg]sound2wem script[/url].
I'm explaining all that because you can make your custom exosuit voice yourself.
You just need to be lucky that someone already created a voice model you like or create your own, but I can't help you with that.

[u][size=3][b]Bugs:[/b][/size][/u]
[list]
[*]You can only have one custom exosuit voice mod installed at a time
[*]The Subnautica PDA voice model slurs sometimes (maybe not enough trained, I don't know)
[*]There are a few callouts that can not be replaced due to a bug in No Man's Sky
[*]The sound files itself have -12 [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LUFS]LUFS[/url]﻿ so are loud enough, I tried louder but in game the volume doesn't
change. Due to a limitation of the game, the new exosuit voice will always be more quiet than the original.[/list]
[b][u][size=3]Installation:
[/size][/u][/b][list]
[*]Vortex should work
[*]For manual installation, extract the contents of the SubnauticaPDA_ExosuitVoice.zip file into your [b]No Man's Sky\GAMEDATA\MODS[/b]
[*][url=https://docs.google.com/document/d/18k5VfvzLXbpBrAGGO7LK30c2Ta_lWQ5F5YgEpuwKZ6M/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.vm4bcr5uj28i]More details here[/url]﻿
[/list][b]
[size=3][u]Special thanks to:[/u][/size]
[/b][url=https://huggingface.co/Aquaaa123]Aquaaa123[/url] for the [url=https://huggingface.co/Aquaaa123/piper-tts-pda-subnautica]Subnautica PDA voice model[/url][url=https://next.nexusmods.com/profile/RangerDulann?gameId=1634]
RangerDulann[/url] for the [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/nomanssky/mods/168?tab=description]Custom voices guide[/url][url=https://github.com/EternalLeo]
EternalLeo[/url] for the [url=https://github.com/EternalLeo/sound2wem]sound2wem script[/url]

name: Expensive Tech Modules
summary: This mod changes the price of tech modules when buying them from a vendor, but without changing the selling price.
author: Zchott
description:
This mod adds a buy markup to all tech modules this means that the vendor will sell you the item for a much higher price, then buying it from you.

The following markup multipliers are added:
C class modules = 1.5x
B class modules = 2x
A class modules = 3x
S class modules = 4x
X class modules = 5x

These changes makes it alot harder to just buy all the modules you want and makes looting modules more rewarding.


This mod makes changes to the following file:
metadata/reality/tables/nms_reality_gcproducttable.mbin
